simple.meaning: אָזַר (ʼâzar) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to belt.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 16 times across 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 2 Kings, Job, Psalms, and 2 more, beginning at 1 Samuel 2:4. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָזַר (H247).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אָזַר (ʼâzar) / H247 is traced through 1 Samuel 2:4, 2 Samuel 22:40, 2 Kings 1:8, Job 30:18 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “The bows of the mighty men are broken.

timeline.evidenceText: “The bows of the mighty men are broken.
For you have armed me with strength for the battle.
They answered him, “He was a hairy man, and wearing a leather belt around his waist.”
My garment is disfigured by great force.
He makes my feet like deer’s feet,
You have also made my enemies turn their backs to me,
to the end that my heart may sing praise to you, and not be silent.
You still the roaring of the seas,
Make an uproar, you peoples, and be broken in pieces! Listen, all you from far countries: dress for battle, and be shattered! Dress for battle, and be shattered!
Make an uproar, you peoples, and be broken in pieces! Listen, all you from far countries: dress for battle, and be shattered! Dress for battle, and be shattered!
I am Yahweh, and there is no one else.
Behold, all you who kindle a fire,
“You therefore put your belt on your waist, arise, and say to them all that I command you. Don’t be dismayed at them, lest I dismay you before them.

definitions.full: H247. azar [ אָזַר ] verb gird, encompass, equip (Talmud id. , Arabic , Aramaic in derivation Lag BN 177 derives from ).
